page: Microsoft Azure EC2eds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. It incorporates 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and maintains compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for external disk requirements. The configuration operates without integrated discrete GPUs.

The hardware design emphasizes memory capacity relative to compute capacity while integrating low-latency local NVMe storage. Because the configuration features 2 dedicated vCPUs, computational throughput is limited compared to compute-dense offerings, making it less appropriate for CPU-bound compiling or heavy parallel batch computation. However, the 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio provides ample headroom for operations requiring higher memory allocations without provisioning unnecessary processor cores. Local scratch capacity is physically bounded by the 118 GB NVMe disk, requiring workloads with broader persistent storage footprints to attach remote storage. Public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

Qualitatively, the resource balance delivers efficiency for mid-tier workloads needing significant working memory alongside local temporary caching. Typical applicable workloads encompass memory-caching nodes, intermediate relational or transactional database deployments, small-scale in-memory stores, ETL batch pre-processing, and backend application servers with modest CPU concurrency requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure EC2eds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 Intel processor under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 118 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage for scratch space and temporary caching, while also supporting Premium Storage configurations. There are no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned to the profile. By pairing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio with dedicated processor cores and local NVMe storage, the instance avoids overprovisioning compute resources for memory-dependent tasks. It is targeted at workloads such as small-to-medium relational database instances, in-memory caching systems, intermediate data processing, and enterprise backend services requiring higher memory footprints relative to overall processing demands.
